question.text: Within how many working days from the close of the issue must publicly offered InvIT units be listed on the stock exchange?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the InvIT Regulations, publicly offered InvIT units must mandatorily be listed on the stock exchange within 6 working days of the close of the issue. The Trap: 12 working days and 3 working days are not the timelines specified for publicly offered InvIT units. The 30-working-days option is wrong for the public-offer scenario asked here — the workbook separately states that privately placed InvIT units shall also be listed within 6 working days of the close of issue, so a candidate cannot rescue option D as the private-placement timeline either. Note: Source — NISM-Series-III-C workbook (January 2026), page 316, which sets the 6-working-day listing requirement from close of issue for publicly offered InvIT units.
